thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: SLO breach for customer `Hearthly` (single-tenant). p99 streaming latency > 12s over last 5m. Errors rising (502/504). Pager: PD-12345. Dash: <http://dash.internal/reports/hearthly/latency?range=5m> :rotating_light:

sre-anna: I'm taking it — oncall paged. Can whoever's online grab mitigation?

oncall-raj: I'm oncall and looking. Noted PD. Adding myself to channel. What's the earliest change that can reduce customer impact?

eng-dan: Noticing a deploy ~30m ago to the dedicated pool for Hearthly (deploy id: deploy-2026-03-14-1023). Pushing to check logs + recent model variant changes.

ml-oliver: I'm seeing KV cache churn and a burst in sequence length for Hearthly requests. Many requests have long system prompts + embedded doc blobs — sequence lengths spike to 16k tokens which is causing streaming stalls and heavy KV eviction.

sre-anna: Reproduced a streaming stall in logs (worker-37). Example snippet: ```
[stream] client_conn=10.2.3.45 req_id=abc123 stall_after_frame=0
frame_write_error: write timeout after 12000ms
stack: runtime/streamer flush -> kv_cache lookup -> kernel exec
```

platform-kim: We can do two quick things: 1) divert traffic to a fallback smaller model to reduce per-token work, 2) temporarily rate-limit the Hearthly tenant to stop the prompt storm. Which should we try first?

eng-dan: I'll flip routing to fallback model now and restart the dedicated pool worker group. Command I'm about to run: ```shell
redwood route set --customer hearthly --model redwood/gpt-small-v2:2026-01 --weight 100 --reason "emergency fallback to reduce tail latency"
redwood infra restart-pool --pool hearthly-dedicated --grace 10s
```

incident-bot: ACTION EXECUTED: route change applied (route-id r-9f3a). Restart job queued (job-8892). See <http://infra.internal/jobs/8892>.

cs-mira: Hearthly is on a bridge with us, they confirm spike started ~15:40 and said they were in processing mode (batching many docs into a single prompt). They're asking for quick mitigation to stop 5xxs.

eng-dan: Restart finished. Rolling restart completed for pool hearthly-dedicated. Observability: p95 now trending down. Still seeing some p99 outliers.

ml-oliver: The root cause seems to be a combination of unusually long prefixes (repeated embedded documents) and high concurrency from a scheduled job at Hearthly. KV cache thrash: many unique prefixes -> no cache hit -> full context recompute every request. Short-term config we can apply: limit max_input_tokens per request for the tenant and enable prefix dedupe in the parser.

sre-anna: Adding temporary rate-limit for Hearthly to give the system breathing room: ```
rl add --tenant hearthly --limit 60r/s --burst 120 --duration 30m --reason "mitigate prompt storm"
```

platform-kim: Enabled conservative batching and prefix cache lock for dedicated pool (flags toggled: `--batching.mode=conservative`, `--prefix.cache.lock=true`). Expecting fewer KV evictions.

incident-bot: METRICS: p95 dropped from 1.8s -> 0.9s, p99 dropped from 16s -> 6.2s in the 10m post-mitigation window. Errors 502 rate reduced by ~78%. Dash: <http://dash.internal/reports/hearthly/latency?range=15m>

cs-mira: Hearthly reports client-side improvement; errors have fallen and streams are coming in. They're keeping their emergency job paused for now.

oncall-raj: Good progress. I'll initiate a formal handoff: I'll own incident until +30m, then hand to next rotation (@eng-dan to follow up on permanent fixes).

ml-oliver: Suggested post-incident action items (to track): 
- enforce tenant-level max_input_tokens and reject huge single prompts (CS/Policy)
- implement prefix dedupe during parse (runtime)
- add tenant-aware cache sizing or soft-eviction thresholds
- add alert rule for sequence-length spikes (p99_seq_len > threshold)
- investigate introducing a per-tenant prompt-shaping helper that truncates or offloads large blobs to embeddings

eng-dan: I'll open follow-up tickets and plan a small patch to the routing layer to automatically fall back on model variants when avg_seq_len > 8k for a tenant. Ticket: RDW-4567.

sre-anna: Status update to #incidents and to the Hearthly bridge: mitigation applied, service stabilized, continuing monitoring. No immediate customer data concerns; CS continuing sync. Will escalate if regressions.

oncall-raj: Handoff note: next oncall please review RDW-4567 and the job logs (job-8892). If tail latency resurges, escalate to runtime-eng and consider temporary customer isolation. I'm leaving the channel + setting PD to low-urg.

cs-mira: Thanks team — Hearthly on the bridge says "thank you, performance improved". We'll keep them in the loop and coordinate the permanent changes. :white_check_mark:

sre-anna: Closing here for now. Will file internal postmortem with timeline and RFO once follow-up patches are scheduled. :memo:
